chunks: And from him, from Ismail ibn Hammam who said:
Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) entered the Kaaba, so he prayed in its four corners; he prayed two cycles in each corner.'

key_terms.النَّبِيُّ: The Prophet, referring to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).
key_terms.الْكَعْبَة: The Kaaba, the cubic structure in Mecca considered the holiest site in Islam.
key_terms.زَوَايَاهَا الْأَرْبَع: Its four corners, referring to the structural corners of the Kaaba.

ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) perform prayer inside the Kaaba?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of praying inside the Kaaba, a practice rooted in the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) entry during the Conquest of Mecca to purify it from idols. The specific detail of praying in the four corners with two rak'ahs each underscores the Kaaba's status as a sacred sanctuary (Masjid al-Haram) where the sanctity of the space elevates the act of worship, a view supported by Shia jurists who cite this as evidence for the validity of individual prayers within the structure.

en.hubeali: And from him, from Ismail Bin Hammam who said,
‘Abu Al-Hassanasws said: ‘The Prophetsaww entered the Kabah, so hesaww Prayed Salaat in its four corners, Praying two Cycles in each corner’.
en.sarwar: 8. It is narrated from him (narrator of previous Hadith) from ‘Isma‘il ibn Hammam who has said the following:

“Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, entered al-Ka‘bah and performed Salat (prayer) in all of its four corners two Rak‘at in each.’”
